result:
I didn't change anything, because I believe this finding is a false positive.

The only place the new code compares a role is `filterUsers` in `utils/filter-users.ts:19`. It has `if (role !== 'ALL' && user.role !== role) return false;`. This doesn't decide what the current user may see or do. It's a UI filter that matches each listed user's role against the role picked in the dropdown. The rule is about access control, so it targets checks on the signed-in user's role.

`<Authorization>` and `checkAccess` can't do this job. Both only test the signed-in user's role against `allowedRoles`. They can't test an arbitrary row from the users list. Forcing the filter through them would be wrong. Rewriting the comparison in a different form, such as `[user.role].includes(role)`, would hide the pattern without fixing anything.

The rest of the diff doesn't check roles. `users-list.tsx` only uses `ROLES` for the dropdown options. The CSV export only prints `user.role` as a cell value.

If a reviewer wants this surface gated, for example so only admins see the Export CSV button, that would be the right use of `<Authorization allowedRoles={[ROLES.ADMIN]}>`. The users page is already admin-only, and you didn't ask for that gate, so I haven't added it. Tell me if you want it.
